Name: PADDR[6:2]
Structural Path: PADDR[6:2] -> s_apb_addr -> PADDIR/GPIOLOCK decode -> protected-write acceptance -> gpio_dir
Attack Scenarios: On a rising `HCLK`, `r_gpio_dir` is updated only inside `PSEL && PENABLE && PWRITE`, when `s_apb_addr` decodes `REG_PADDIR`; `r_gpio_lock[0] == 0` passes `PWDATA`, otherwise the RTL writes zero. `apb_gpio_gpio_dir_cone.PADDR` supplies the address decode that distinguishes `REG_PADDIR` from the other GPIO registers. An attacker can alter `apb_gpio_gpio_dir_cone.PADDR` during an otherwise valid APB write so that a transaction intended for another register is decoded as `REG_PADDIR`. The supporting RTL chain is `apb_gpio_gpio_dir_cone.PADDR -> apb_gpio_gpio_dir_cone.gpio_dir`. The presented `PWDATA` is captured into `r_gpio_dir`, changing pad directions without the intended direction-register access.
Justification: For `PADDR[6:2]`, one authoritative exploitation route shows that the signal selects which APB register receives a write. Because an altered address slice can redirect an otherwise legal transaction to PADDIR, the documented behavior makes `PADDR[6:2]` relevant to compromise of `gpio_dir`.
